key_gap: vs baseline: the pure outside-view baseline is the gold standard here (class named, distribution read, plan placed at 3rd percentile, Aurora reclassified as 2/60 tail, deal structured on the class, adjustment bounded by the team's own ceiling) — the routed dual pass reached full content parity first-pass and added what the pure style leaves implicit: a P1 input-provenance audit (Marta's deal-shaped incentive, vendor commitments as the forecast's most interested parties), the weakness-gate class-selection test, and a priced failure branch (fixed $1.5M price vs 21-month reality kills the vendor). The non-routed v5 AI lost this case 3.6–4.9 by factor-calibrating the anchor (16 mo) instead of forecasting from the distribution; the routed pass closes that to parity.
learning_signal: On estimate/predict tasks with a checkable base-rate distribution in frame, the distribution must be the forecast basis — a completion contract forcing class-named / base-rate-stated / inside-outside-separated converts the pure style's move into a reproducible first-class pass and kills the factor-on-anchor failure mode; provenance of the inside estimate (who benefits from the number) is what lets the agent refuse it without appearing contrarian.
suggested_improvement: Keep the outside-view pass routed on estimate/predict signatures with given base rates (dual-route with m044); extend its checklist with (a) interested-party provenance on the inside estimate (beneficiary named per input), (b) the class-selection test as a standing weakness gate (structural membership features + adjustment bounded by the team's own ceiling), and (c) percentile placement of the plan (z-score AND empirical count) stated in WHY before any alternatives are generated — the percentile placement is what the v5 WHY missed.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style executed its core move and failed on class selection — it adopted the industry survey (n=412, surface label 'e-commerce project') over the firm's own 9-build history, ported the 1.9× factor across classes, and forecast 9–12 months against a true 5–7-week class (2.9). The routed run never routed the outside-view module (router historical evidence: style loss on this signature) and reached the same verdict the v5 AI found emergently — narrow class as the forecast basis — through dual-route m044+m070 (consultant-incentive provenance, feature-match ledger grading) plus the divergence rule (6× gap flags misclassification, not bias) as a standing gate; the trap is now avoided at routing level, not by luck.
learning_signal: Reference-class forecasting's dominant failure is class selection, not distribution reading: two candidate classes with opposite distributions in plain view are decided by structural membership features (platform, team, spec status, integration novelty), never by sample size or surface label — and the router should treat the style's loss record on a signature as evidence against routing it, converting the trap into a protective gate.
suggested_improvement: Keep the outside-view module OUT of the route on signatures whose historical record shows the class-selection trap (m097-NEG-01), and install the class-selection gate as a standing protective check: name the deciding structural features, grade each candidate class against them, refuse cross-class factor porting (P10), and apply the divergence rule (inside estimate far outside a candidate class flags misclassification, not bias). Add the re-test trigger on scope change to the m044 pass checklist.
